faq.q: How long does Earth take to go round the Sun?
faq.a: About 365 days, 5 hours and 49 minutes. That is a little less than 365 and a quarter days.
asks: How long is a year really?

faq.q: Why do we add a day every four years?
faq.a: Each year leaves about a quarter of a day over. Four quarters make one whole day, so every fourth year gets 29 February.

faq.q: Why is adding a day every four years too much?
faq.a: The real year is about 11 minutes shorter than 365 and a quarter days. Those minutes pile up to about 3 days every 400 years.
asks: Why do leap years need fixing?

faq.q: Which century years are leap years?
faq.a: Only those that divide exactly by 400, like 1600, 2000 and 2400. 1700, 1800, 1900 and 2100 are not leap years.

faq.q: Who made the leap year rule?
faq.a: The every-four-years rule came from Julius Caesar's calendar, which began in 45 BCE. The century rule was added in 1582, in the calendar named after Pope Gregory the Thirteenth.

facts: A Gregorian calendar year averages 365.2425 days, very close to the solar year of about 365.2422 days.
Century years are leap years only if they divide exactly by 400, so 2000 was a leap year and 1900 was not.
